status: frozen before any new source-localization or target-class ratings; local ordering only, not independent authenticated preregistration
question: Are two securely localized manuscript glyphs in the same physical graphical class, different classes, or unresolved?

source.document: BnF Francais 3758, item 104; Chatillon to Servien, 3 August 1635

source_gate: Readable primary-source pixels, exact image or capture SHA256, dimensions, URL, capture type and orientation must be recorded. A viewer derivative is not claimed to be an archival master.
Both target IDs must be linked to exact bounding boxes and full line context. Do not identify them by their shared text label or expected deciphered output.

Prefer the pinned historical inventory with source-image linkage. If unavailable, a fresh source-only localization may reconstruct a new coordinate map only when the full physical ordering and neighboring anchors uniquely establish the locations; keep this distinct from recovery of historical coordinates.

If row identity, physical grouping, target boundary, token ordering or source-image association remains ambiguous, retain all candidates and report the target identity unresolved. Do not select the candidate that best fits a desired class.
The class comparison for the named pair is admissible only after the source gate passes.
observer_isolation: A new observer receives no inherited conversation and only anonymous randomized crops plus the feature rubric. No historical class names, target IDs, plaintext, key values, computational counts, source-localizer verdict or desired conclusion. Observer must not inspect other research files.
feature_rubric: Number and closure of loops or enclosed regions
Attachment and relative placement of stems, returns and crossing strokes
Number and relative placement of detached marks
Boundary of each glyph and possible overlap with neighbors
Record slant, scale and thickness separately from topology; do not infer pen stroke order
controls: Before target ratings, freeze two byte-identical duplicate-crop positive controls and two visibly distinct-topology negative controls using unrelated glyphs from the same source image. Keep control truth, crop coordinates, hashes and randomized presentation order in a coordinator registry not given to the observer. If two suitable distinct-topology controls cannot be selected securely, stop rather than invent ground truth.
pixel_policy: Use native pixels and, if needed, nearest-neighbor display enlargement; retain native crops and line context. No generative enhancement, stroke retouching, selective erase, rotation or source replacement. Unreadable loop closures or attachments remain uncertain regardless of enlargement.

decisions.same_physical_class: Every critical topology feature is readable and agrees; scale, slant or thickness differences alone are not sufficient to split classes.
decisions.different_physical_class: At least one readable stable topological difference is explicitly identified.
decisions.unresolved: Any critical feature or source localization is uncertain, observer controls fail, or provenance/source gate fails.
decisions.control_gate: All duplicate controls must be same and all securely distinct-topology controls must be different. Failure invalidates target interpretation; preserve the raw response without repairing the rubric.

required_outputs: Source/capture hashes and metadata; source-localization evidence and uncertainties; frozen crop registry and control truth; exact blinded prompt and raw observer response; disclosed AI assistance. Publish only cleaned text/metadata unless image redistribution rights are verified.
limits: Physical graphical agreement does not establish historical cipher outputs or a semantic key. The coordinator knows prior calculations; blinding applies to the fresh observer, not the entire project. Preserve PR4/PR5 and their earlier protocol amendment. No old computational experiment replay.
amendments: Any change after a source-localization or class response must be separately recorded with its timing and already exposed information.
